controls: The intake records explicit Creative Production route selection, exact board destination and asserted approval metadata; that route choice is the confirmation and is not requested again.

A user-confirmed decision records the exact board, revisions, item IDs, snapshotted references, selected item and supported translation tokens. Every preview and release manifest binds that decision and records each selected token as visibly applied or mechanically not applicable; it cannot claim that a token influenced bytes when it had no target. classes.content: The workflow never scans the Studio archive, mailbox or workspace broadly: the professional enumerates exact current sources and any exact prior communications. There is no internal sampling or row/column cap; every selected supported file is snapshotted and processed in full. For prior communications, local code replaces mechanically detectable email addresses, phone numbers, tax identifiers, bank-account identifiers and case numbers with stable placeholders. Model phase 1, in a dedicated session, receives only those stripped prior communications; names, organizations, addresses, locations, roles and identifying combinations may still be visible because semantic pseudonymization requires them. It returns one complete derivative per item plus a contextual identity mapping that is stored locally and never routed downstream. Model phase 2, in a fresh session, receives only the candidate derivatives and reviews residual contextual identification; it does not receive originals, stripped inputs, mappings or the first transcript. Only a ready result unlocks generation. After acceptance, transient stripped inputs and both dedicated history packets are deleted with a digest-bound receipt; original snapshots and the combined identity map remain owner-controlled. Model phase 3, generation, receives selected current-source snapshots, task instructions, Studio/audience/channel information and only the cleared pseudonymized derivatives. Model phase 4, claim assurance, receives only the answer contract, proposed contribution and selected current-source snapshots. Model phase 5, editorial assessment, receives only the proposed contribution and completed claim assurance. Model phase 6, visual assessment, receives only accepted copy, the exact visual manifest and exact rendered files. Claim, editorial and visual packets exclude every prior communication and identity map. Codex and Cowork use the same shared core mechanics. The optional Creative Production boundary is Codex-only and receives only accepted public slide copy and minimal Studio visual context as separately described. This is purpose-preserving pseudonymization, not anonymization or local-only model processing, and session separation is operator-attested rather than a provider-authenticated file sandbox or model-call receipt.
classes.purpose: Assess whether a professional development warrants communication and prepare source-backed studio-formatted drafts and visual stories for review

classes.content: Local DOCX inspection produces formatting metadata, style identifiers and the file path without extracting document text. These metadata can identify the studio. The selected model may read selected metadata, studio identity, preferences, the selected logo, the proposal, synthetic previews and review decisions. Direct visual inspection of a selected document may also expose its text. If example text needs interpretation, the isolated stripping, pseudonymization and independent review steps of Professional Communication apply. The private standard retains configuration, assets and approval; a subsequent report receives only presentation settings and logo, without examples or communications history. That report’s accounting data follows its separate process. No archive scan, sending or automatic upload to Mparanza. Local storage does not make model processing offline or automatically anonymous. No model-service call is made by the local helper. Font availability and user visual acceptance are not proved by byte-integrity checks. Unobserved communications settings are labelled default proposals in first setup, not learned from examples. The setup or revision proposal can also expose the complete prior or proposed communications profile: studio voice, letter, email, web and social conventions, field provenance and adoption metadata. Those saved conventions are not prior communications text.

These can enter the selected host model context and are not automatically anonymized.

de: Der Umfang ist die Auswahl der Fachperson, nicht das Kanzleiarchiv.

Die Fachperson wählt jede aktuelle Quelle und jede optionale frühere Mitteilung aus: Die Funktion durchsucht weder Archiv noch Postfach und verwendet keine Stichprobe oder Zeilen-/Spaltenbegrenzung; jede ausgewählte unterstützte Datei wird vollständig verarbeitet. Bei früheren Mitteilungen ersetzt lokaler Code zuerst erkennbare E-Mail-Adressen, Telefonnummern, Steuerkennungen sowie Konto- oder Aktennummern. Ein eigener erster Durchlauf sieht den vollständigen gefilterten Text und kann weiterhin Namen und Kontextdetails sehen; er erstellt je Datei eine vollständige pseudonymisierte Kopie. Ein unabhängiger zweiter Durchlauf sieht nur die Kandidaten und sperrt die Generierung, wenn wesentliche Identifizierbarkeit verbleibt.

Die Generierung erhält alle ausgewählten aktuellen Quellen, Zielgruppe, Kanäle, Kanzleiprofil und nur freigegebene Kopien. Die Anspruchsprüfung erhält Vertrag, Entwurf und alle aktuellen Quellen; die redaktionelle Prüfung nur Entwurf und Prüfungsergebnis; die visuelle Prüfung nur freigegebenen Text, Manifest und gerenderte Dateien. Originale und Zuordnung bleiben im privaten Arbeitsbereich; gefilterte Eingaben und temporäre Pakete werden gelöscht. Der History-Connector ist gesperrt: Die Fachperson exportiert und wählt exakte Dateien. Werden weitere Belege benötigt, kommen neue Quellen in einen neuen Lauf; öffentliche Recherche startet nur nach Auswahl, mit generischen Suchanfragen und exakten Snapshots.

Dies ist Pseudonymisierung, keine Anonymisierung. Der gemeinsame Kern von Vera und Lucia wendet dieselbe Grenze an; nur Codex kann optional bereits freigegebenen öffentlichen Folientext und minimalen visuellen Kontext an Creative Production senden, niemals Quellen oder Historie. Die Sitzungstrennung wird vom Operator bestätigt und ist keine provider-authentifizierte Dateisandbox.
en: The boundary is the professional's selection, not the firm's archive.

The professional selects every current source and any prior communication: the function does not scan the archive or mailbox and applies no sampling or row/column cap; it processes every selected supported file in full. For prior communications, local code first replaces recognizable email addresses, phone numbers, tax identifiers, and account or case numbers. A dedicated first pass sees the complete stripped text and may still see names and contextual details; it creates one complete pseudonymized copy per file. An independent second pass sees only the candidate copies and blocks generation if material identification remains.

Generation receives every selected current source, audience, channels, firm profile, and only the cleared copies. Claim assurance receives the contract, draft, and every current source; editorial review receives only the draft and assurance; visual review receives only accepted copy, the manifest, and rendered files. Originals and the mapping remain in the private workspace; stripped inputs and temporary packets are deleted. History connectors are blocked: the professional exports and selects exact files. If more evidence is needed, new sources are added to a new run; public research runs only when selected, with generic queries and exact snapshots.

This is pseudonymization, not anonymization. Vera and Lucia’s shared core applies the same boundary; only Codex may optionally send already-approved public slide copy and minimal visual context to Creative Production, never sources or history. Session separation is operator-attested, not a provider-authenticated file sandbox.
es: El perímetro es la selección del profesional, no el archivo del despacho.

El profesional elige cada fuente actual y cualquier comunicación anterior: la función no explora el archivo ni el correo y no aplica muestras ni límites de filas o columnas; procesa íntegramente cada archivo seleccionado compatible. En las comunicaciones anteriores, el código local sustituye primero correos, teléfonos, identificadores fiscales y números de cuenta o expediente reconocibles. Una primera pasada dedicada ve el texto completo ya filtrado y todavía puede ver nombres y detalles de contexto; crea una copia seudonimizada completa por archivo. Una segunda pasada independiente solo ve las copias candidatas y bloquea la generación si queda identificación relevante.

La generación recibe todas las fuentes actuales seleccionadas, público, canales, perfil del despacho y solo las copias aprobadas. La comprobación de afirmaciones recibe contrato, borrador y todas las fuentes actuales; la revisión editorial solo borrador y comprobación; la visual solo texto aprobado, manifiesto y archivos renderizados. Originales y tabla de correspondencia permanecen en el espacio privado; las entradas filtradas y los paquetes temporales se eliminan. El conector del historial está bloqueado: el profesional exporta y elige los archivos exactos. Si hacen falta más pruebas, se añaden nuevas fuentes a una nueva ejecución; la investigación pública solo empieza si se elige, con consultas genéricas y copias exactas.

Es seudonimización, no anonimización. El núcleo compartido de Vera y Lucia aplica el mismo límite; solo Codex puede enviar opcionalmente a Creative Production texto público ya aprobado y un contexto visual mínimo, nunca fuentes ni historial. La separación de sesiones es una declaración del operador, no un entorno aislado de archivos autenticado por el proveedor.
fr: Le périmètre est la sélection du professionnel, pas les archives du cabinet.

Le professionnel choisit chaque source actuelle et toute communication antérieure éventuelle : la fonction ne parcourt ni les archives ni la messagerie et n'applique aucun échantillon ni plafond de lignes ou colonnes ; chaque fichier sélectionné et pris en charge est traité intégralement. Pour les communications antérieures, le code local remplace d'abord les e-mails, téléphones, identifiants fiscaux et numéros de compte ou de dossier reconnaissables. Un premier passage dédié voit le texte complet ainsi filtré et peut encore voir des noms et détails contextuels ; il crée une copie pseudonymisée complète par fichier. Un second passage indépendant ne voit que les copies candidates et bloque la génération si une identification importante subsiste.

La génération reçoit toutes les sources actuelles sélectionnées, le public, les canaux, le profil du cabinet et seulement les copies validées. La vérification des affirmations reçoit le contrat, le projet et toutes les sources actuelles ; la revue éditoriale seulement le projet et la vérification ; la revue visuelle seulement le texte accepté, le manifeste et les fichiers rendus. Originaux et table de correspondance restent dans l'espace privé ; les entrées filtrées et paquets temporaires sont supprimés. Le connecteur d'historique est bloqué : le professionnel exporte et choisit les fichiers exacts. Si d'autres preuves sont nécessaires, de nouvelles sources sont ajoutées à un nouveau run ; la recherche publique ne part que si elle est choisie, avec requêtes génériques et instantanés exacts.

C'est une pseudonymisation, pas une anonymisation. Le noyau partagé de Vera et Lucia applique le même périmètre ; seul Codex peut envoyer facultativement à Creative Production le texte public déjà validé et un contexte visuel minimal, jamais les sources ni l'historique. La séparation des sessions est attestée par l'opérateur, pas par un bac à sable de fichiers authentifié par le fournisseur.
it: Il perimetro è la selezione del professionista, non l'archivio dello Studio.

Il professionista sceglie ogni fonte corrente e ogni eventuale comunicazione precedente: la funzione non esplora l'archivio o la posta e non applica campioni o limiti di righe e colonne; per i formati supportati elabora per intero tutti i file selezionati. Sulle comunicazioni precedenti, il codice locale sostituisce prima email, telefoni, codici fiscali e numeri di conto o pratica riconoscibili. Un primo passaggio dedicato vede i testi completi così ripuliti e può ancora vedere nomi e dettagli di contesto; crea una copia completa pseudonimizzata per ogni file. Un secondo passaggio indipendente vede solo le copie candidate e blocca la generazione se resta un'identificazione rilevante.

La generazione riceve tutte le fonti correnti selezionate, pubblico, canali, profilo dello Studio e soltanto le copie approvate. La verifica delle affermazioni riceve contratto, bozza e tutte le fonti correnti; la revisione editoriale solo bozza e verifica; quella visuale solo copia approvata, manifest e file renderizzati. Originali e mappa restano nel workspace privato; gli input ripuliti e i pacchetti temporanei vengono eliminati. Il connettore per lo storico è bloccato: il professionista esporta e sceglie i file esatti. Se serve nuova evidenza, aggiunge nuove fonti a un nuovo run; la ricerca pubblica parte solo se scelta, con query generiche e snapshot esatti.

È pseudonimizzazione, non anonimizzazione. Il nucleo condiviso di Vera e Lucia applica lo stesso perimetro; solo Codex può inviare facoltativamente a Creative Production il testo pubblico già approvato e il minimo contesto visuale, mai fonti o storico. La separazione delle sessioni è attestata dall'operatore, non è un sandbox di file autenticato dal provider.

security_controls.control: Workspace initialization requires explicit user confirmation, asserted owner and retention owner, owner-only permissions and an exact bound path outside the Git repository or published roots. Run creation commits from a private staging directory, cleans incomplete same-run staging state on retry, and every mutating command uses a non-blocking operating-system writer lock plus atomic file replacement.

Preparation accepts only regular non-symlink selected files, copies them into owner-only run storage, records byte size and SHA-256, rejects duplicate identities, and binds the complete intake plus source register to one digest. Review, render, package, validation and delivery gates recompute that digest and fail when a source, history item, profile snapshot, logo, register field or intake field is missing or changed.

The professional must enumerate every exact prior communication in the intake; the workflow does not scan Studio storage or account history. Local preparation extracts complete readable text and replaces mechanically recognizable email addresses, phone numbers, Italian tax codes and labelled tax IDs, valid IBANs and labelled account IDs, and labelled case numbers using fixed auditable patterns before model use. The reversible mapping stays in owner-only local storage and is excluded from the isolated model packet. One isolated model pass receives only those stripped documents and must produce one complete pseudonymized derivative per selected item plus a separate contextual identity mapping. Recording requires exact input binding, every selected history ID once and in order, preservation of every locally inserted placeholder, rejection of normalized mapped-identity reappearance, rejection of newly introduced mechanically detectable identifiers, the bundled prompt hash, affirmative model-assessed semantic dimensions, derivative hashes, owner-only mapping storage and a distinct host session. It stages rather than releases those derivatives. A second fresh model session receives only the candidate derivatives and must clear contextual residual identification without seeing originals, maps, stripped inputs or the first transcript. Only a ready, complete, digest-bound assessment promotes the derivatives. The recorder then deletes transient stripped inputs and both dedicated history packets, records their hashes in a cleanup receipt, retains original snapshots and the identity map locally, and routes only projected derivative paths and hashes to generation. Contribution recording fails when either record or cleanup receipt is missing, when any derivative or map changes, or when a session is reused. These checks materially reduce exposure but do not certify anonymity or a provider-level file-access sandbox; contextual identities may be visible to the selected runtime in the isolated first pass.

Generation receives selected current-source snapshots and only the independently cleared pseudonymized history derivatives. Before claim assurance, editorial assessment or visual assessment, a deterministic builder writes one digest-bound allow-list of exact file paths, sizes and SHA-256 hashes for that phase. Claim assurance receives the answer contract, proposed contribution and selected current sources; editorial assessment receives the contribution and completed assurance; visual assessment receives accepted copy, the exact manifest and rendered files. The corresponding recorders fail on a missing, stale, changed or mismatched packet. Every downstream packet rejects history derivatives, history records, identity maps, stripped inputs and history-session packets. Editorial packet preparation validates the completed claim assurance, including answer-contract conformity and explicit professional-judgment routing, before writing or replacing the packet.

Exhaustive JSON Schemas reject unknown intake and contribution fields; a recursive normalized-key guard rejects password, passcode, PIN, OTP, cookie, session-cookie, token, API-key, client-secret, private-key, secret-key and credential fields from model contributions.

Each model contribution is stored with an exact version snapshot and bound to recomputed input and contribution digests plus explicit model provenance. Every gate compares the current workbench with its version snapshot. Review events require user confirmation and locally asserted reviewer identity; superseding a returned or rejected contribution creates a new version, archives prior derived render and package artifacts under the earlier contribution version, and invalidates prior decisions. Rendered-output decisions additionally bind the exact visual-manifest digest.

Selected prior communications can create only a reviewable profile proposal. A Studio with no selected history may receive a complete first proposal from an explicit format brief, supplied brand facts and Vera defaults, but cannot use observed-history provenance. Every profile field is labelled observed-history, user-supplied or Vera-default with exact evidence coverage; unsupported channels cannot silently become observed Studio practice. Persistence requires a fresh accepted studio-profile review, versions the prior profile and logo asset in the same exact bound workspace, preserves the field basis and adoption record, and writes a format digest over brand, asset and profile. Later unchanged runs snapshot the stored profile and logo and reject conflicting brand or logo intake unless an explicit profile-revision basis was supplied.

Deterministic renderers operate only after required semantic review acceptance, reject text that cannot fit declared safe geometry, measure circular headers, footers and contact rails, verify extractable PDF text without silent truncation, and record exact output, layout, font and visual-manifest hashes. The isolated visual assessment must bind every carousel slide and each rendered PDF with its exact page count before release. Packaging preserves the contribution's reviewed public source text and URL instead of injecting a generic profile note. It requires user-confirmed acceptance of the current render digest when present, writes validation_pending, and validation of publishable communication additionally requires user-confirmed acceptance bound to the exact package digest. For an already accepted no_publish contribution, validation instead checks the six internal record kinds, exact accepted recommendation text and current semantic review event bindings; no packaged-output approval is invented. An explicit package rejection remains blocking. The resulting no_publication_recommended status cannot authorize external delivery. External receipt recording rechecks current outputs and receipt bindings, requires the approved exact destination and user-confirmed visible evidence, and cannot overwrite prior evidence.

The optional Creative Production handoff is emitted only for an explicitly selected route and a contribution already accepted by the independent editorial assessor. It recomputes input and immutable contribution integrity, binds the visual story and each exact slide to SHA-256 digests, limits shared context to public slide copy and minimal Studio visual identity, and labels every direction non-publishable. Rendering is blocked until a current user-confirmed selected-board decision or explicit fallback exists; the decision snapshots references and binds board and translation digests. The final manifest records supported tokens as applied or not applicable and its verifier recomputes that classification from the exact accepted story.

A live editorial assessor is accepted only when its exact provider, model and prompt-template SHA-256 has a current digest-bound result on the blinded product-reviewed high-bar corpus, with no false-ready critical case. History pseudonymization, derivative-only privacy review, generation, claim assurance, live editorial assessment, benchmark qualification and visual assessment record distinct host session IDs and exact prompt hashes; the provenance explicitly states that it is operator-attested and not provider-authenticated. Each contribution is also bound to an answer contract and a separate full-material-claim assurance record that covers every contract dimension and keeps source identity, semantic support, reasoning and professional judgment distinct. Deterministic code scores fixed benchmark outcomes and enforces record closure; it never assigns semantic quality, contextual identifiability or source support.

Selected examples and the logo are snapshotted into the bound private workspace. Adoption rechecks proposal digest, studio identity, prior-standard hash, all selected input hashes and both short/long preview hashes. The common writer versions previous standards. Reviewer and visual acceptance are operator assertions, not authenticated proofs.

model_processing.destination: OpenAI model processing used by Codex
Anthropic model processing used by Cowork

external_boundaries.content: Published shared package names and version constraints plus ordinary package-index request metadata. No client files, prompts, case data, credentials, or generated work are sent by this runtime installer.
controls: Only published shared core and explicitly selected OCR recipes are installed; package names are never derived from client material or prompts.

Host network denials stop package retrieval. Retry only the same declared setup after the host user or administrator authorizes registry access; never change host network settings or use an alternate installer to evade a denial.

Readiness probes the managed CPython 3.12 interpreter locally with isolated Python and site loading disabled, checks completed installation metadata, then checks the selected declared package versions and component imports in that interpreter. Recipe revisions, backend bytes and historical platform labels do not block a compatible environment. Compatible reuse leaves installation receipts unchanged; actual missing or incompatible dependencies require serialized repair.
All three products and their modules use the same environment. Optional OCR requires approval and is then retained in that environment. A shared environment is not a boundary between client matters.
external_boundaries.destination: Python Package Index (PyPI) or the package index configured for the active Python interpreter
external_boundaries.purpose: Prepare the published shared Vera, Clara and Lucia core requirements and explicitly approved optional OCR in one user-scoped Python 3.12 environment per operating-system host.
external_boundaries.retention: Packages remain in one fixed user-scoped environment outside plugin source and client folders until explicitly removed. The default location is ~/.local/share/mparanza/runtime/venv on macOS and Linux, and LOCALAPPDATA/mpr/venv on Windows; MPARANZA_RUNTIME_ROOT may override the parent. Enabled OCR remains enabled across later core updates. Package-index request-log retention is controlled by the configured index. Failed updates invalidate the readiness receipt and require repair before execution; this shared environment has no retained generations.

external_boundaries.content: The fixed CPython 3.12 version request, operating-system and architecture selection, and ordinary download request metadata. Setup does not read client files or add prompts, case material or generated reports to this request.
controls: Use an installed CPython 3.12 when available; otherwise use uv or automatically download the published uv 0.12.10 wheel, verify its pinned SHA-256, and provision private CPython 3.12 without changing system Python or shell profiles.
Probe the selected interpreter before creating the dependency environment; never fall back to executing workflows with another Python minor version.
A failed download or interpreter probe stops setup; existing environments and client files remain intact.
external_boundaries.destination: PyPI files.pythonhosted.org for the pinned uv bootstrap, and Astral python-build-standalone CPython distributions on GitHub
external_boundaries.purpose: Provision the single supported CPython 3.12 interpreter when it is absent, automatically bootstrapping uv if needed
external_boundaries.retention: When uv must be bootstrapped, the bootstrap executable and private interpreter remain inside shared runtime storage until removed. Download request-log retention is controlled by the providers.

external_boundaries.content: Random installation UUID and opaque capability, Vera/host/runtime versions, platform and workflow technical IDs, failed stage, complete available technical diagnostic chains and measurements, explicit missing-measurement reasons, retry IDs and actual recovery outcomes. No professional helper stdout, client documents, case text, user prompts or arbitrary task logs. Known path, email and credential patterns are removed from technical messages; this mechanical filter does not establish semantic privacy. The host agent must select technical evidence without unrelated personal/client material. The remote channel does not read local files. Failed helpers retain complete stderr privately on disk; stderr may include unrelated private/client text and is read by the selected host model for semantic review under its existing account. Raw stderr is not forwarded to Mparanza. Only reviewed relevant technical diagnostics, linked by the original report UUID, are submitted as supplemental evidence. Professional stdout is not captured. Managed helpers also send source-bound exception classes, OS error numbers, package-relative stack coordinates, developer-authored error templates and missing required option names automatically. Dynamic exception/argument values, locals, professional stdout and arbitrary source excerpts are not part of these structured events. Process-session UUIDs, persistent operation UUIDs and optional keyed digests of existing run/input-receipt identities bind attempts without disclosing receipt fields or raw client-input hashes. Actual worker interpreter/platform fields are separate from the reporter's interpreter. Capture completeness, pending semantic review, exact remedy/retry events and host verification of the original task remain distinct evidence states; a structured event is not a semantic diagnosis.
controls: Only closed technical transport schemas are accepted; unknown fields and arbitrary recovery commands are rejected.
The fixed HTTPS transport refuses redirects. Reporting failures retain the outbox and do not discard professional outputs.
The remote connector is independent of local command-process startup. If the host cannot expose/connect it, no successful report is claimed.
Only two built-in setup/preparation retries may execute automatically, once per remedy revision. Client documents, ACLs and security settings are not changed.
A published update is not recovery. The failed operation must actually execute successfully before that installation delivery closes.

Supplemental diagnostics require ownership of the original report and matching execution metadata; they are stored separately and cannot change the original report UUID, delivery status or remedy revision. Raw local diagnostic files can only be removed by acknowledging a matching recorded supplement.
Actionable remedies target an explicit original report. Each delivery uses its own applicable revision; a different report with the same generic signal does not inherit that remedy.

A cached actual connector status permits only the two fixed retries for an existing matching local receipt and latest report. It performs no direct HTTP polling or identity adoption. Missing local receipts cannot be fabricated to authorise a retry.

A helper success records readiness. Host AI verification of the original task and inputs is required for all recovered outcomes, including setup/startup. Delayed failures cannot reopen an already recovered episode.
Failed fixed retries retain complete stderr privately for semantic review. Raw recovery stderr is not automatically transmitted.

An explicitly selected MPARANZA_INCIDENT_DELIVERY=local-only setting blocks automatic client HTTP transport for this execution while preserving local evidence. Incident queues are durably marked and not automatically flushed later; this does not make model-provider processing local-only.
external_boundaries.destination: Mparanza HTTPS operational-incident API and Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint
external_boundaries.purpose: Diagnose observed execution/setup failures, return installation-specific remedies and receive actual recovery outcomes
external_boundaries.retention: Local capability, pending reports and receipts persist outside client folders. The service retains incident, report, remedy and outcome records; no automatic deletion period is enforced. Status access is scoped by the opaque capability. Pending diagnostic pointers and raw stderr persist in the private incident directory until a matching actual recorded supplementation receipt is acknowledged; unsuccessful review or delivery retains them. Supplementation never replaces the original recovery episode or reopens recovered records. Recorded original/outcome receipts can acknowledge only their exact local queued UUID without replacing the local capability or saved connector identity. Remedy revisions are retained from the surviving migration revision onward; overwritten legacy revisions are not reconstructed.

security_controls.control: Setup validates package-relative selections and installs the published shared recipe. No package names or dependency instructions are accepted from client documents.
security_controls.on_violation: An unknown module, missing requirements file, invalid target, or failed dependency validation stops the helper instead of executing it in a partial environment.

security_controls.control: One fixed environment is located outside plugin source and client folders. An exclusive operating-system installation lock waits for running managed Python readers, which hold a shared lease through a startup hook. Setup removes the ready receipt before mutation and restores it only after pip check and component validation. Failed setup leaves execution unavailable until repair. Symlink roots, locks and metadata are rejected. The installer is launched from base Python to avoid self-deadlock. This lease is concurrency protection, not a security sandbox. Other historical environments are not automatically deleted. State metadata normally uses atomic replacement. Only EXDEV or Windows error 17 falls back under the same installer lock to a single-link regular-file write with full-byte writes and fsync. Failed writes attempt to restore existing metadata or remove a newly created file; the ready receipt remains invalid until setup succeeds. This fallback is local and does not add a recipient or payload.
security_controls.on_violation: A target creation or validation failure returns a bounded setup error and the requested helper is not run.

security_controls.control: The Windows archive launcher probes a callable interpreter and package entrypoint without changing aliases, registry, execution policy or client folders. The archive helper checks package readability before setup and supplies an explicit task UUID to every managed archive command. Recovery requires reconnecting the selected existing archive root; tasks do not silently adopt each other's configuration. Diagnostics return bounded package/startup status rather than client documents.
security_controls.on_violation: An unreadable package or invalid session stops before runtime setup and archive commands.

security_controls.control: For the six explicitly supported assured modules, the launchers verify the complete package inventory and stable regular-file bytes against the embedded build-generated SHA-256 index. Symlinks, reparse entries, special files, extra directories/files, missing or changed code and unstable reads stop preparation. Unchanged hardlinked package code is materialized into a fresh private OS temporary directory; each copied file is re-read and must have one physical link, then the unchanged component integrity validator must pass. The managed installation and aliases are not modified. The copy contains indexed product code/assets, not client documents, credentials, workflow reports or dependency environments. This local index detects package drift; it is not a publisher signature, a signed origin attestation or proof of installed-host acceptance. Successful code copies remain in OS temporary storage for normal OS cleanup. The root-level host .in_use directory is non-executable bookkeeping: only ASCII numeric, ordinary single-link regular marker files are excluded from the product inventory. Nested directories, links, reparse points and non-numeric names there are rejected. Marker contents are not read, executed, transmitted or included in a recovery copy; host markers and installed product files are not modified.
security_controls.on_violation: Preparation failures and host permission denials stop execution. A failed private copy is removed; no installation chmod/unlink/manual repair, alternate sandbox or relaxed component validation is permitted.

security_controls.control: The parent Vera launcher reports a negative exit code or 137/247 as forced termination. It writes execution_failure.json only inside the selected workflow context output directory or its normalization/sample subdirectories; without that matching context it logs only. The diagnostic stores workflow/run identifiers, exit status and an explicit statement that memory exhaustion is not established by the exit code. It makes no model calls or network requests.
security_controls.on_violation: A worker failure remains failure; diagnostic persistence errors are logged rather than converted into a success.

security_controls.control: The standalone Python bootstrap passes uv only declared host paths, locale, proxy, CA and cache settings, preserving original environment-name casing. Unrelated token/API-key variables and inherited UV_*, VIRTUAL_ENV, CONDA_PREFIX, PYTHONHOME and PYTHONPATH are excluded; private UV_PYTHON_* and UV_CACHE_DIR values are set by the bootstrap. The same environment is used for interpreter discovery and its local probe.
security_controls.on_violation: Undeclared environment names are absent from every bootstrap child process.

security_controls.control: The built-in incident dependency-setup retry uses the shared host/runtime environment allowlist, named runtime/state locations and recovery recursion guard instead of inheriting unrelated user tokens and keys.
security_controls.on_violation: Undeclared environment names are absent from the child environment.

security_controls.control: When the maintained launcher itself runs under Python -I -B, it restores only its own resolved scripts directory for sibling technical-diagnostic imports. It does not add the caller working directory. Helper execution, diagnostic retention and explicit incident delivery policy remain unchanged.
security_controls.on_violation: The maintained launcher must stop rather than resolving technical diagnostics from the caller working directory.

external_boundaries.content: Random installation UUID and opaque capability, Vera/host/runtime versions, platform and workflow technical IDs, failed stage, complete available technical diagnostic chains and measurements, explicit missing-measurement reasons, retry IDs and actual recovery outcomes. No professional helper stdout, client documents, case text, user prompts or arbitrary task logs. Known path, email and credential patterns are removed from technical messages; this mechanical filter does not establish semantic privacy. The host agent must select technical evidence without unrelated personal/client material. The remote channel does not read local files. Saved anonymous connector authorization exchanges a random code with a PKCE verifier, client ID and fixed incident resource; the host saves access/refresh tokens. The server stores token/code hashes, technical callback metadata and a random connection UUID. No personal account signup, user profile, email or client-file permission is involved. Failed helpers retain complete stderr privately on disk; stderr may include unrelated private/client text and is read by the selected host model for semantic review under its existing account. Raw stderr is not forwarded to Mparanza. Only reviewed relevant technical diagnostics, linked by the original report UUID, are submitted as supplemental evidence. Professional stdout is not captured. Installation-preparation failures submit only a fixed technical message, exception type/errno, or the indexed package-relative file name and expected/observed SHA-256 values for a content mismatch. No altered file contents or professional files are read for this report. Managed helpers also send source-bound exception classes, OS error numbers, package-relative stack coordinates, developer-authored error templates and missing required option names automatically. Dynamic exception/argument values, locals, professional stdout and arbitrary source excerpts are not part of these structured events. Process-session UUIDs, persistent operation UUIDs and optional keyed digests of existing run/input-receipt identities bind attempts without disclosing receipt fields or raw client-input hashes. Actual worker interpreter/platform fields are separate from the reporter's interpreter. Capture completeness, pending semantic review, exact remedy/retry events and host verification of the original task remain distinct evidence states; a structured event is not a semantic diagnosis. Current reporting-process version, protocol capabilities and server last-seen time are retained per process session, separately from historical failure versions; they do not establish that all conversations updated. Native-host binding, when invoked, accepts a random host UUID and scoped capability plus an optional explicit native-app label at the same incident service. Only the host capability hash is retained server-side. Stable app-profile UUIDs are derived from host UUID and app label; reporter-instance UUIDs may be task-local and do not count physical computers, plugin copies or people. App grouping grants no additional client status or outcome access. Operator views retain each original report, supplement, outcome and retry event with its actual reporting owner and server receipt time; missing historical task identity is not reconstructed. The native stdio identity bridge verifies its indexed entry, reporter, technical collector and product metadata, then executes an isolated temporary reporter snapshot using existing Python without installing dependencies. Its tool accepts only an existing reporter capability and sends host proof to the fixed register endpoint; it never returns the device key or copies the reporter key into the host identity file. Native broker version/session observations are retained separately from guest reporter and failure-worker observations. When native tools are not exposed in cloud Cowork, the saved remote connector continues to report under its distinct connection identity and physical-host linkage remains unknown; no device controls or folder permissions are expanded automatically. Native-helper failures return source-bound exception classes, errno or HTTP status, package-relative frames and developer-authored templates. Dynamic diagnostic values are not returned; unavailable capture is explicit. This bridge does not return raw stderr or device keys. The central recovery agent may request named technical evidence surfaces through a diagnostic-request remedy. The host AI replies with reviewed technical facts, the original report UUID and request revision. Original-task availability is represented by technical booleans, not task text, client identifiers or file contents. A resume remedy communicates a diagnosed correction to the existing authorized workflow; it does not carry executable code. Technical requests, response UUIDs, applicable revisions and their observed status are retained with the original episode. The central agent may implement and deploy incident-related software fixes through reviewed source and green CI under Fabio’s explicit recovery authorization; it does not receive professional case files or gain user-host permissions. Handled Studio Archive exceptions log their active traceback locally before returning the existing error JSON, allowing the same source-bound collector and host semantic review to retain their actual cause. The operator derives diagnostic publication, exact owner/report/revision receipt and reply states, the existing 15-minute deadline and reporting-owner last service contact from retained records. These delivery facts do not establish physical-host availability, diagnosis or original-task recovery. The operator also projects exact delivery, retry and original-task outcome evidence for all actionable remedy kinds, including software updates. Its 15-minute attention cadence is not an execution timeout. A local alert renderer uses technical incident facts and an AI-reviewed blocker, accountable next action, reason and scheduled check. An optional operator-maintained device label is accepted only with a recorded exact-device verification reference; it is not inferred from the recipient, OS or reporter identity. Rendered operator alerts may include opaque machine/case codes and a verified operator-device label, but no client contents, raw diagnostics, personal identifiers or credentials. The renderer neither sends email nor accesses the registry or client files. It rejects stale followup reviews and cannot assign an unreceived or overdue remedy back to the uncontacted Vera. Recovered labels require matching actual original-task success evidence; incomplete historical bindings remain unknown. The shared API also exposes a separate public workflow-testing endpoint: an allowlisted map of pipeline IDs to testing levels and baseline metadata, without incident details, computer IDs, run IDs or user feedback. Its reset is operator-only and does not change incident records. Native workflow transport supplies the same existing host proof during registration when it is available. The shared managed launcher also reports handled PDF recovery failures and subsequent attempts for journal-sampling and journal-bank-reconciliation. It projects fixed strategy/check identifiers, pass/fail/replay flags and attempt/readable-row counts only; PDF text, amounts, paths, adapter code and free-text rationale remain local. Supplements reuse the original report identity across process sessions and cannot certify original-task recovery. Other products carry the shared implementation but do not expose these journal workflows. Bank PDF inspection failures and subsequent corrections are linked per source, independently of journal failures. The bank source digest used in the episode key stays in local reporting state and is not added to transmitted evidence. Other bank statements cannot inherit that extraction recovery. The same native bridge also exposes the fixed task-usage operations documented by the workflow-usage service, with a verified usage-client/catalogue snapshot and task-scoped persistence. Those operations use the existing installation/computer capabilities internally and do not accept credentials, paths, commands or client documents. Error results include SQLite symbolic error codes where available; no raw database contents or diagnostic values are returned. A separate local execution service accepts a published component helper, its argument list, an idempotent job UUID and the retained usage-task UUID. It verifies an indexed code snapshot and invokes the existing managed runtime, without accepting shell expressions or external executable paths. Arguments, complete helper stdout/stderr, job status and cancellation evidence remain in private local execution storage; these can contain case data and are not included in incident HTTP payloads. On a result request, the helper output and status enter the selected host model context through the normal recorded output boundary. Internal collection of stdout is not counted as a model send. Existing subordinate-worker submissions keep their own recording boundary. Native cancellation reads the local OS parent-process graph only to terminate that job and descendants; the graph is neither returned to the model nor uploaded. Native execution and the fixed incident identity/usage broker are separate services.
controls: Only closed technical transport schemas are accepted; unknown fields and arbitrary recovery commands are rejected.
The fixed HTTPS transport refuses redirects. Reporting failures retain the outbox and do not discard professional outputs.
The remote connector is independent of local command-process startup. If the host cannot expose/connect it, no successful report is claimed.
Only two built-in setup/preparation retries may execute automatically, once per remedy revision. Client documents, ACLs and security settings are not changed.
A published update is not recovery. The failed operation must actually execute successfully before that installation delivery closes.

The remote MCP requires OAuth access tokens for the fixed incident resource. Authorization uses S256 PKCE, exact registered callbacks and a single-use five-minute code. Refresh tokens rotate and a replay revokes the grant; raw OAuth credentials are never placed in model prompts or stored server records.

Supplemental diagnostics require ownership of the original report and matching execution metadata; they are stored separately and cannot change the original report UUID, delivery status or remedy revision. Raw local diagnostic files can only be removed by acknowledging a matching recorded supplement.
Actionable remedies target an explicit original report. Each delivery uses its own applicable revision; a different report with the same generic signal does not inherit that remedy.

A cached actual connector status permits only the two fixed retries for an existing matching local receipt and latest report. It performs no direct HTTP polling or identity adoption. Missing local receipts cannot be fabricated to authorise a retry.

A helper success records readiness. Host AI verification of the original task and inputs is required for all recovered outcomes, including setup/startup. Delayed failures cannot reopen an already recovered episode.
Failed fixed retries retain complete stderr privately for semantic review. Raw recovery stderr is not automatically transmitted.

Actual cached connector status reconciles only readiness hints bound to existing local report receipts. Readiness becomes action-required evidence rather than recovery; already recovered matching hints are cleared and unlinked hints are retained. No remote receipt is fabricated and no case inputs are inferred.

Before reporting an installation-preparation failure, the preflight verifies the reporting script, preflight script and product metadata against a stable build index, then snapshots them in a fresh private temporary directory and executes the reporter in isolated Python. Original-installation, cwd and PYTHONPATH imports are excluded. Damaged workflow code does not run. Unverifiable reporting components require the independent connector; queued delivery never implies recorded or recovered.

A diagnostic reply requires ownership and exact original execution metadata, plus a retained diagnostic-request revision targeting that original report. A late reply cannot answer a newer request. A diagnostic exchange cannot be marked recovered.

Operator publications can require the inspected current revision. Identical applicable remedies are idempotent and do not create another retry episode. Resume instructions use existing verified workflow tools and ordinary professional gates; service text is never executed as a command.

An explicitly selected MPARANZA_INCIDENT_DELIVERY=local-only setting blocks automatic client HTTP transport for this execution while preserving local evidence. Incident queues are durably marked and not automatically flushed later; this does not make model-provider processing local-only.

The shared implementation binds registrations, OAuth resources, task events, report signatures, feedback and update downloads to one product. Existing unmapped installations and receipt schema 1 remain Vera. Physical-computer identity is shared, while usage catalogues and testing epochs are separated by product.

PDF recovery evidence uses the existing durable outbox and exact original-report supplementation, including local-only delivery. Readable partial results and independent workflow gates survive incident-service failure. Frozen extraction is explicitly unqualified and never generates a recovered outcome.

When a native execution supplies its retained task UUID, newly created local incident entries and operation identities carry that scope. Failure/progress delivery and success recovery select only that task. Older queued evidence and receipts are neither relabelled, removed nor transmitted by the task. The scope stays local and adds no external report field; unscoped maintenance remains a separate operation.
external_boundaries.destination: Mparanza HTTPS operational-incident API and Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint
external_boundaries.purpose: Diagnose observed execution/setup failures, return installation-specific remedies and receive actual recovery outcomes
external_boundaries.retention: Local capabilities, pending reports and receipts persist outside client folders. In tested Cowork task containers this filesystem is task-local; the saved host connection retains its separate random UUID and credentials. Access tokens last one hour; rotating refresh grants expire after 90 idle days and can be revoked. Token/code hashes and incident records have no automatic deletion period. Access requires the local capability or the saved connector token, with explicit capability proof before linking local reports. Pending diagnostic pointers and raw stderr persist in the private incident directory until a matching actual recorded supplementation receipt is acknowledged; unsuccessful review or delivery retains them. Supplementation never replaces the original recovery episode or reopens recovered records. Recorded original/outcome receipts can acknowledge only their exact local queued UUID without replacing the local capability or saved connector identity. Remedy revisions are retained from the surviving migration revision onward; overwritten legacy revisions are not reconstructed. Native execution requests, stdout/stderr and status remain in private user-scoped diagnostic job directories until local administrative deletion; no automatic expiry is implemented. Verified code snapshots contain code only and remain in OS temporary storage for normal cleanup.

security_controls.control: Only a matching random installation capability can retrieve incident status or record its recovery. Stored keys are SHA-256 digests; server validation never echoes invalid input.
security_controls.on_violation: Reject without returning another installation record.

security_controls.control: Remote data cannot supply executable commands. Only reviewed built-in action IDs are supported; retries use argv without a shell and preserve integrity guards.
security_controls.on_violation: Reject unsupported actions and keep the incident open.

security_controls.control: OAuth discovery has fixed server URLs, public clients use mandatory S256 PKCE and exact registered callbacks, and every grant is bound to the incident resource and sole incident scope. Token/code hashes are stored, access expires in one hour, refresh rotates, reuse commits grant revocation, and foreign report outcomes require a proven local link. Caller-supplied metadata URLs are never fetched.
security_controls.on_violation: Reject invalid authorization, token or resource proof without returning caller inputs or another connection record.

security_controls.control: Built-in recovery children receive the shared host/runtime environment allowlist, explicit named runtime/state locations and the recovery recursion guard. Unrelated user tokens and keys are not inherited.
security_controls.on_violation: Undeclared environment names are absent from the child environment.

security_controls.control: Diagnostic collection resolves portable Archive contexts through the maintained identity, manifest and input-receipt verifier. PDF recovery evidence and killed-worker diagnostics use that run's verified output directory; a different run's output is rejected. Context hydration is local and adds no external payload fields.
security_controls.on_violation: Retain the original execution outcome and report unavailable diagnostics without attributing another run's evidence.

external_boundaries.content: For every run of the 13 selected Vera pipelines, Archive automatically prepares a schema-3 proof request containing product, receipt UUID, plugin version, canonical report SHA-256, existing Vera userID (installation_id), Archive run ID and report revision. The operational transport authenticates existing installation credentials and requires its existing verified machine link. Ordinary connection metadata also reaches Mparanza. No report body, outgoing payloads, source paths, source hashes, row counts, source values, prompts or model outputs are submitted. Verification supplies the receipt ID, report hash, Vera userID, Archive run ID and revision together.
controls: Only the fixed 13-pipeline scope generates new automatic Vera reports. Every selected execution gets a report, including full exposure and incomplete measurements. Start/end writes control collection; no agent-authored report input or substantive-work decision is used.

Vera records its own outgoing CLI, MCP and model-worker payloads locally before sending them, independently of host hooks and transcripts. Private internal results and MCP app-only metadata are excluded. The terminal Archive write freezes the local report immediately; a later result from a still-running operation is withheld if its pinned run or revision has closed or changed.

Vera schema 3 requires authenticated installation credentials and an existing physical-machine link. The public anonymous stamping route cannot issue this schema. userID, Archive run ID, revision and report hash are included in the Ed25519 signature.

The request uses one fixed HTTPS operational endpoint. Additional fields, mismatched owner identity, changed retry evidence, wrong-product records and verification mismatches are rejected. Local outgoing payloads are never sent.

Retries retain identical report bytes, UUID, version and revision. Professional artifacts are checked before and after updating only the reserved reporting artifacts in the Archive seal. Ordinary Archive use retries pending receipts and interrupted terminal reporting without re-executing professional work.

An explicit local_only option or local onboarding marker suppresses the proof request but keeps the report. Network or identity failures retain a pending receipt without invalidating the professional work. Host permission denials remain binding.

Verification proves the stored report hash, authenticated Vera installation/machine binding, Archive run, revision and server time. It does not identify a natural person or establish provider-side receipt, correctness of measurements, analytical correctness or GDPR compliance.
Historical schema-1 and schema-2 receipts remain readable through their existing routes; the authenticated Archive proof does not depend on a separate workflow-usage link.
external_boundaries.destination: Mparanza's fixed HTTPS Vera run-receipt endpoint and public verification page
external_boundaries.purpose: Authenticate the existing machine Vera userID and bind the hash of each selected Archive run report to that run, revision and server time.
external_boundaries.retention: The server retains the proof fields, server timestamp, signature and signing-key identity, with a unique userID/run/revision binding, without an automatic deletion period. Reports, exact Vera outgoing payloads, local database and receipts remain inside the local Archive run until the studio removes them. Deleting a server proof makes later server verification unavailable.

security_controls.control: The local collector accepts complete transport envelopes only when their exact digest matches a producer declaration. Selected row-field origins and private review-packet digests are retained locally, independently of send events; constructing them does not count as disclosure. A changed envelope, unknown private review packet or unregistered metadata parent cannot inherit the original declaration. Partial text reads cannot inherit complete-artifact lineage.
security_controls.on_violation: The report retains the outgoing payload hash and marks source accounting incomplete; it does not fabricate an unsent remainder or prevent ordinary result delivery merely because provenance is unavailable.

security_controls.control: Both client and server enforce the same closed receipt request schema, and the server's Pydantic model forbids every unregistered field.
security_controls.on_violation: The request or response is rejected before a proof is accepted or written locally.

security_controls.control: Automatic Archive stamping and verification use fixed Mparanza HTTPS endpoints; operational credentials authenticate the existing Vera installation. The transport refuses redirects. The older generic receipt client retains its explicit loopback test option.
security_controls.on_violation: The client aborts before making a network request.

security_controls.control: The server signs the exact minimal record with Ed25519, including authenticated Vera userID, Archive run and revision for schema 3. A unique userID/run/revision binding prevents a second proof for different bytes. Conflicting receipt retries are rejected atomically; no report or source data are stored.
security_controls.on_violation: Missing keys make the service unavailable, invalid signatures are not returned as verified, and conflicting retries are rejected.

security_controls.control: Receipt routes cap body size and operation rates. Archive stamping additionally authenticates installation credentials and requires the retained verified device link; anonymous requests cannot create schema-3 proofs.
security_controls.on_violation: Oversized or excess requests receive an explicit 413 or 429 response without creating a receipt.

workflow-usage.display_name: Pipeline usage, outcomes and user satisfaction

external_boundaries.content: The existing installation capability authenticates closed-schema events: random run and event UUIDs, sequence, catalog pipeline ID, host, observed product version, timestamps, explicit user/synthetic/agent-test classification and started/resumed/completed/failed/cancelled state. Optional links contain only an existing signed receipt UUID/report digest or an owned incident report UUID. Run ownership, single-run receipt binding and the retained signature are checked server-side. The original stamping service does not attest the identity of the author of a report. The service receives no task text, client identity, filenames, source data, prompt or professional output. Existing connection metadata and rate limiting apply. Saved connector identity is not inferred to be a native computer. Native senders also present the existing anonymous native-computer capability and observed native app when available. The server retains the established computer binding; unlinked guests remain unlinked until an actual native proof is received. Connector-owned runs can obtain the bounded per-run proof described above; run-specific computer bindings are used by counts and completion indicators. No personal account information or hardware identifier is collected.
controls: Events are durably queued before transport and acknowledged by exact UUID, owner, sequence and hash. Interruptions stay outcome unknown; repeated submissions are idempotent.
Synthetic and agent-test runs are excluded from user metrics. Studio Archive is infrastructure and cannot be selected as a rated process.
The host AI selects the primary process and observes actual task completion. Counters and hashes do not assert professional correctness or independent model delivery.

The operational client honors an explicitly selected local-only HTTP delivery setting for this execution; this does not change synthetic-run exclusion, rating authorization or model-provider processing.

The shared implementation binds registrations, OAuth resources, task events, report signatures, feedback and update downloads to one product. Existing unmapped installations and receipt schema 1 remain Vera. Physical-computer identity is shared, while usage catalogues and testing epochs are separated by product.

Authenticated event acknowledgements and run status expose the original owner's proven Computer ID and whether an actual signed receipt is linked. Missing linkage remains explicit and returns bounded follow-up instructions. Neither reporting gap changes the professional outcome or authorizes broader host access.

When local HTTPS is unavailable, the authenticated connector can stamp the exact retained receipt request for an owned run. The allow-list admits only receipt UUID, product/version, schema and report digest. It returns the same signed proof; a separate verified receipt event links it to the original run. No report or source contents are transmitted.

Connector-owned workflow acknowledgements return a random 15-minute proof scoped only to binding that original run to a native computer. The existing native helper adds its private computer capability and observed app. The server stores only the ticket hash, checks product, expiry and app, rejects re-binding, and never replaces the original owner or associates all runs from one saved connection with one computer. The proof cannot authorize other reporting operations. Exact event replay obtains a fresh proof without another event.

Ordinary startup and outcome delivery select only the retained task UUID. Scoped flush and connector inspection return only that task's pending events/count; unrelated retained events cannot make its delivery pending. Startup context exposes only a diagnostic backlog count, without unrelated task IDs. Whole-outbox maintenance is separate; historical event bytes and owner/hash acknowledgement checks are preserved.

The native plugin service exposes fixed task start, observed event, status and task-scoped retry operations using the existing local reporter and computer identity. It persists events in the existing user-scoped database without requiring the chat shell to write outside its project. It accepts no client file paths, shell commands, replacement credentials or global queue flush. Storage failures retain structured operation/error evidence and cannot certify delivery or invalidate professional output.
external_boundaries.destination: Existing Mparanza HTTPS operational-incidents API and saved veraIncidents OAuth connector
external_boundaries.purpose: Measure which user processes run and their observed outcome; link existing signed model-data receipts and technical reports without copying their professional content
external_boundaries.retention: Task events, optional feedback and receipt links remain in the service until administrative deletion; no automatic expiry is implemented. Local queued events and acknowledgements remain in the existing private per-installation state directory. Lifecycle events exclude client documents and professional output. Optional feedback stores only the comment deliberately supplied by the user; its contents are not automatically anonymized. Host-link tickets expire after 15 minutes; their hashes and established run-to-computer bindings remain until administrative deletion. The raw short-lived proof is returned only in an authenticated acknowledgement and not in status or operator projections.

external_boundaries.content: The actual 1–5 integer score, up to 2000 characters of optional user-authored comment, source (chat or form), random event UUID and existing task binding. Nothing is copied automatically from professional context. The host asks once after delivery; no response is unrated. A low score offers one optional question about what failed or was expected.
controls: The user supplies the score/comment for submission or clicks Invia valutazione; that action is the choice, with no second confirmation questionnaire.

The form uses a run-specific capability in its URL fragment; the page contains no task information, and the capability permits rating only that run. The exact pending answer is retained for retry, and operator rendering escapes comments.

Comments are untrusted data for AI review, never instructions or executable commands. Feedback never changes public testing levels or closes incidents. Completed pipeline runs feed a separately resettable computer-based testing counter and never close incidents.
external_boundaries.destination: Mparanza task feedback through the same authenticated connector/client or the per-run hosted form
external_boundaries.purpose: Collect the user’s actual 1–5 stars and optional comment about the delivered result
external_boundaries.retention: Task events, optional feedback and receipt links remain in the service until administrative deletion; no automatic expiry is implemented. Local queued events and acknowledgements remain in the existing private per-installation state directory. Lifecycle events exclude client documents and professional output. Optional feedback stores only the comment deliberately supplied by the user; its contents are not automatically anonymized.

external_boundaries.content: Only catalog pipeline IDs, four testing-level names and counting epoch UUID/time are public. The service privately groups completed runs by proven anonymous computer IDs: the owner-designated computer counts as agent testing, other computers as professional use. Stars, comments, report digests, client documents, task prompts, computer IDs, run IDs and capabilities are not in this response. The owner convention counts computers, not authenticated people; completion does not certify professional correctness. No model call is made by this public projection.
controls: Both server receipt and event completion time must follow the baseline; old delayed deliveries do not repopulate a reset.
Native computer IDs deduplicate apps and reporter instances. Unlinked completions stay pending until proven linkage; explicit test fixtures on other devices do not count as professionals.
The public response is an allowlisted projection of status-only fields; reset is available only to the server operator.
external_boundaries.destination: Mparanza public GET /api/vera/testing-status and Vera function catalogue
external_boundaries.purpose: Automatically show testing levels from concluded pipelines after an explicit fresh baseline
external_boundaries.retention: Counting epochs and underlying retained events persist until administrative deletion. A reset preserves history and starts new public counts.

security_controls.control: Existing installation/OAuth authorization scopes task writes and reads; closed schemas reject unrelated fields. UUIDs, event order and retained hashes enforce retry identity.
security_controls.on_violation: Reject the event without changing task evidence.

security_controls.control: A usage receipt link must match the retained report digest/version and a valid server signature.
security_controls.on_violation: Reject the unverified link and retain the task without receipt evidence.

security_controls.control: The feedback route checks a per-run random capability, bounds the body and comment, and never exposes task data on the public form. Operator HTML escapes text.
security_controls.on_violation: Reject the request or render it only as literal text.

security_controls.control: The public endpoint returns only the four-state map and epoch metadata. Device/run identities and feedback remain private; no public reset route exists.
security_controls.on_violation: Unknown or missing fields are not included in the public projection.

security_controls.control: The indexed native service snapshots the usage client and catalogue with the reporter, technical collector and product metadata. Fixed arguments select one retained task UUID; the existing owner/event/sequence/hash checks govern acknowledgement and replay. Native results do not return installation or computer keys.
security_controls.on_violation: Reject unsupported operations and extra fields before task persistence; preserve queued events and expose source-bound storage errors without raw diagnostic values.
